meta.title: Who really said "A woman knows by intuition, or instinct, what is best for herself"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No — Marilyn Monroe never documented this line. Wikiquote lists it as misattributed and of unknown origin, with no primary source anywhere.

answer.label: Not Marilyn Monroe — a misattribution of unknown origin
answer.authorName: Unknown — falsely credited to Marilyn Monroe
answer.sourceLine: There is no record of Marilyn Monroe writing or saying this line in any film, interview, letter, or her memoir. Wikiquote lists it under “Misattributed” ↗, noting it is “of unknown origin and date” and reached Monroe only through self-help books and social media. Its true author is not documented.

source.excerpt: A woman knows by intuition, or instinct, what is best for herself.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ places the line in its “Misattributed” section and states it is “of unknown origin and date.”
Quote-aggregator pages such as BrainyQuote ↗ and QuoteFancy ↗ repeat the Monroe credit but supply no citation.
No published book, film transcript, or interview by Monroe — including her memoir My Story — has ever been shown to contain this sentence.
source.excerptNote: Circulated as a standalone caption on quote-aggregator sites and social media; no surrounding context or original publication has ever been produced.
source.rightsNote: The wording’s origin is undocumented, so no copyright or public-domain status can be responsibly asserted. Because it cannot be tied to any known author or first publication, we mark the rights “uncertain” rather than claim it is public domain.

author.name: Marilyn Monroe
author.heading: About the wrongly-credited figure
author.bio: Marilyn Monroe (born Norma Jeane Mortenson) was one of Hollywood’s most enduring stars, known for films such as Some Like It Hot and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes. Decades after her death she became a magnet for feel-good and “empowerment” quotations pinned to her image with no source. This intuition line is one of many such attributions that cannot be traced to anything she actually said or wrote.

misattribution.heading: The misattribution
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook social-media misattribution: a tidy empowerment line attached to a famous, much-quoted woman with nothing behind it.

items.why: Repeated across quote sites and merchandise, but Wikiquote ↗ files it under “Misattributed” and notes it is “of unknown origin and date.” It appears in none of her films, interviews, letters, or her memoir.
No earlier source in any other writer’s work has been identified; the sentence surfaces only as an uncredited caption, so its real origin remains unknown.

misattribution.truthLine: Best evidence: this is not a documented Marilyn Monroe quotation — it is an unsourced line of unknown origin ↗ later attached to her name.

context.heading: Why it sticks to her
lead: Marilyn Monroe has become one of the internet’s largest “quote magnets”: short, affirming sentences about womanhood, confidence, and self-trust are routinely stamped with her name and photo because the pairing feels plausible and shares well. The absence of any citation is exactly what you would expect from a caption that originated online rather than in a documented source.
In this case even the aggregators that credit her offer no book, film, or interview — and the most careful reference, Wikiquote, explicitly flags the line as misattributed and of unknown origin.
context.pull: A tidy empowerment line, a famous face, and no source in sight — the signature of a manufactured quote.
